The LSCC had a design tip speed of 153 m/s.
Laser anemometer measurements were acquired at 7 stations through the impeller and 4 stations in the vaneless diffuser.
The laser anemometer technique was able to accurately measure pitch angles near the shroud, with agreement within 2 degrees compared to five-hole probe measurements.
The CFD solution used a grid with 137 streamwise points, 71 spanwise points, and 41 pitchwise points, with clustering near the blade surfaces.
The CFD solution underpredicted the maximum velocity deficit in the wake and the spanwise extent of the wake compared to the experimental data.
The wake was observed to shift toward the pressure side of the blade passage as the flow progressed downstream.
The laser measurements provided details of the flow within the blade boundary layers that were not captured in previous investigations.
The LSCC facility was designed to generate a flow field aerodynamically similar to high-speed subsonic centrifugal compressors.
Polystyrene latex spheres with a mean size of 0.8-0.95 μm were used as the seeding material for the laser anemometer measurements.
The encoder system generated 200 counts per blade pitch to track the circumferential location of the velocity measurements.
